title: Pseudospin Dynamics of Charge Order
abstract: Charge order is conventionally viewed as a static modulation of the electronic density, despite growing experimental capabilities to probe and manipulate its nonequilibrium evolution. In contrast to spin-ordered systems, a microscopic framework for charge-order dynamics and its control under external driving remains largely underdeveloped. Here, starting from an extended Hubbard model, we derive an effective pseudospin model in which the charge-ordered state maps onto staggered pseudospin order. The resulting charge-order dynamics is governed by Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert-like equations for the pseudospins, closely analogous to those of a bipartite antiferromagnet. We show that an external electric field directly controls the staggered pseudospin order and, above a threshold field, drives coherent reversal of the charge-order polarity by destabilizing collective pseudospin excitations. Our results establish the charge pseudospin as a microscopic dynamical degree of freedom for coherent switching and control of charge order, providing a charge-sector analogue of the well-established framework for spin-order dynamics in spintronics.
summary: This work develops a pseudospin model for charge order, treating it as a dynamic variable rather than a static modulation. By deriving dynamics analogous to those in antiferromagnets, the authors show that an external electric field can coherently switch the charge-order polarity. This establishes a charge-sector analogue to spintronics, opening pathways for electrical control of charge states.
main_problem: The paper addresses the lack of a microscopic framework describing the non-equilibrium dynamics and external control of charge order, contrasting with the view of charge order as static.
main_result: It establishes the charge pseudospin as a dynamical degree of freedom, showing that an external electric field can drive a coherent reversal of the charge-order polarity above a critical threshold.
method: The authors derive an effective pseudospin model from the extended Hubbard model and analyze its dynamics using Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-like equations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the extended Hubbard model, which is mapped onto an effective pseudospin Hamiltonian. The dynamics are governed by pseudospin operators ($	au_i$) analogous to those in bipartite antiferromagnets.
key_observables: Staggered pseudospin order (N), charge-order parameter ($N_z$), and the critical switching field ($E_c$).
important_parameters: External electric field ($E$), doping/chemical potential ($h_z$), and coupling constants ($J_z, J_\perp$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the strong charge-ordering regime and employs semiclassical mean-field dynamics approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the charge order and the switching of its polarity by an external electric field. Figure 2 shows the time evolution of the charge-order vector during field-driven switching.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the effective pseudospin Hamiltonian from the extended Hubbard model, establishing the LLG-like dynamics, and finally analyzing how an external electric field drives coherent switching by destabilizing collective pseudospin excitations.
why_interesting: The direct analogy drawn between charge-pseudospin dynamics and well-established spin-order dynamics (spintronics) provides a powerful, transferable theoretical framework for understanding electrical control in charge-ordered materials.

(a) Charge order (CO) with alternating doubly occu- pied and empty sites in a half-filled extended Hubbard model with U < ZV , in which an intracell electric dipole p0 emerges due to the accompanying inversion-symmetry breaking. (b) Switching of the CO polarity by an external electric field that couples to the intracell dipoles and thereby acts as a staggered field on the two pseudospin sublattices. Here, doubly occu- pied (empty) sites are represented by orange (green) pseu- dospin arrows, and the CO state corresponds to staggered pseudospin order on the A and B sublattices.
